farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ ٱلْفِيلِ﴾.
He says: have you not been told about the Abyssinians? They had marched against the House and the people of Mecca. When they were at Dhū al-Majāz, they passed by a herdsman of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and drove off his camels. He mounted his riding animal and came to Mecca, cried out the cry of alarm, and then told them the news. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib leapt onto the back of his horse and caught up with them. Two men of Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt said to him: Go back [149/a] — they were friends of his. He said: By Allah, I will not leave until I take my camels or am taken with them. So they said to Aṣḥama, the chief of the Abyssinians: Give them back to him, for he will take them [back] in the morning [anyway]. So he returned with his camels and told the people of Mecca the news. They stayed for some days seeing nothing; then ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib went back to their place, and behold, they were as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: "كالْعَصْف المَأْكُولِ" (like devoured straw). Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, had sent against them birds carrying in their beaks stones like sheep droppings; the bird would let go of the stone and it would not miss its man's head, and it would come out of his backside; so they killed them all. ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib took of the yellow and the white — meaning gold and silver — as much as he wished, then returned to the people of Mecca and told them; and they went out to their camp and [plundered] what was in it. [Translator's note: the source has «فانتبهوا» (they became aware of), apparently for «فانتهبوا» (they plundered); translated by the latter.]

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَبَابِيلَ﴾.
It has no singular, like الشماطيط, العباديد and الشعارير [Translator's note: all words for scattered groups]; for none of these is a singular used. Al-Ruʾāsī — and he was trustworthy and reliable — claimed to me that he had heard its singular: إِبَّالة, with no yāʾ in it. And I have heard among the Arabs one who says: "ضِغث على إبَّالة" (a handful [of grass] on top of a bundle), meaning: plenty on top of plenty. As for «الإيبالة», it is the surplus of fodder that is on top of the load of a donkey or camel; it is like "plenty on plenty", and a load on top of a load. So if someone said: the singular of «الأبابيل» is إيبالة, it would be correct, as they said: دينار, دنانير. And one of the grammarians — al-Kisāʾī — said: I used to hear the grammarians say: أبوك, like العِجّول and العجاجيل. [Translator's note: «أبوك» is as printed; the parallel with «عجّول / عجاجيل» indicates the singular «إبّول».]

farraa:4-4.t: And it is said: ﴿سِجِّيلٍ﴾ is like baked brick, cooked from clay. Al-Kalbī said: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to me; he said: I saw in the house of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib about a qafīz [Translator's note: a dry measure] of those stones, black and streaked with red.

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَعَصْفٍ﴾.
«العصف» is the tips of the crop before it ripens and forms ears.
